issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Meal differs between the problem statement / solution and the template. The UML in problem_statement.md and the solution implementation declare the constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first). The template's Meal.java declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first). Because example usage in Main (in the template) and the exercise description use the name-first order, students who follow the statement will attempt to call new Meal("name", new String[]{...}) and get a mismatch with the template constructor, causing compilation errors or confusion about the correct parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the template Meal.java to match the problem statement and solution: declare it as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and assign fields accordingly (this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients;). Ensure the example usages in Main and any comments use the same parameter order (name first) to avoid compile-time mismatches.
